summary: This special Ramadan lecture was held in a mosque. The ustaz explains the manners and meaning of the mosque, then tells how the house of Allah built by Ibrahim without idols became a place of idols. Amr ibn Luhay al-Khuza'i, a respected religious leader, brought the idol Hubal from Sham and set it at the Kaaba. The idols spread through the pilgrims, together with the idols of five righteous men from Nuh's time that were dug up again. The ustaz then describes the world's darkness before revelation, including cruelty in Rome, Persia, India, China and Africa, and how Islam reached the Malay world. He closes with the Prophet SAW in the Cave of Hira in Ramadan and the light of the Quran descending.
keyPoints: The Kaaba was built by Prophet Ibrahim for worshipping Allah with no idols.
Amr ibn Luhay al-Khuza'i was the first to bring an idol, Hubal, to the Kaaba.
Idols spread through pilgrims and through the five idols of righteous men of Nuh's time: Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr.
The whole world was then in the darkness of ignorance and cruelty.
The Quran came down in Ramadan as a light to illuminate that darkness.

chapters.title: Opening in the mosque
chapters.summary: The special Ramadan session is held in a mosque, and the ustaz introduces a topic about the mosque.

chapters.title: Manners and meaning of the mosque
chapters.summary: The mosque is the house of Allah, a place of prostration. The ustaz teaches entering with the right foot and reciting the supplication for the doors of mercy.

chapters.title: The Kaaba, a qibla without idols
chapters.summary: In Ibrahim's time there were no idols and the Kaaba was only the qibla, not something worshipped.

chapters.title: How the idols came in
chapters.summary: The ustaz asks how a place of prostration to Allah became a place of idols, and introduces the first to bring them.

chapters.title: Amr ibn Luhay al-Khuza'i
chapters.summary: He was a trader who often traded to Sham before the Prophet SAW was born.

chapters.title: Admiring Sham
chapters.summary: He admired the splendour of the people of Sham and thought they were great because they worshipped idols.

chapters.title: Hubal brought to Mecca
chapters.summary: He brought home the great idol Hubal on a camel and set it before the Kaaba.

chapters.title: A respected leading figure
chapters.summary: Because he was a respected leader, people slowly accepted the idol.

chapters.title: Idols spread through the Hajj
chapters.summary: Pilgrims from distant tribes carried home idols such as Lat, Uzza and Manat.

chapters.title: Ibrahim's religion changes
chapters.summary: People without knowledge simply followed their leader, until the whole Arabian peninsula was full of idols.

chapters.title: The five idols of Nuh's time
chapters.summary: In a dream Satan told him of five idols inherited from Nuh's time, who were originally righteous men.

chapters.title: Statues of the righteous become worshipped
chapters.summary: Statues were made to remember the righteous, but later generations worshipped them. The ustaz mentions Surah Nuh verse 23.

chapters.title: Idols spread and the date idols
chapters.summary: The five idols were dug up and carried to various places. Small idols were sold, and some were made of dates and then eaten.

chapters.title: A world in darkness
chapters.summary: The ustaz describes cruelty in Rome, Persia, India, China and Africa, and the burying of baby girls in Mecca.

chapters.title: Islam reaches the Malay world
chapters.summary: Islam arrived through traders who showed good character until many embraced Islam and mosques were built.

chapters.title: The light of the Quran descends
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW in the Cave of Hira in Ramadan received the light, and knowledge is the first matter in the first revelation.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions Surah Nuh verse 23, which names the idols Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr.
dalil.translation: saying, “Do not renounce your gods! Do not renounce Wadd, Suwa, Yaghuth, Yauq, or Nasr!”

dalil.context: The ustaz recites the verse that Ramadan is the month in which the Quran was sent down.
dalil.translation: It was in the month of Ramadan that the Quran was revealed as guidance for mankind, clear messages giving guidance and distinguishing between right and wrong. So any one of you who is present that month should fast, and anyone who is ill or on a journey should make up for the lost days by fasting on other days later. God wants ease for you, not hardship. He wants you to complete the prescribed period and to glorify Him for having guided you, so that you may be thankful.

sirah.era: Before revelation: the origin of idols in Mecca
sirah.summary: This lecture explains how idols entered the Kaaba before the Prophet's birth and the state of the world before revelation.

events.label: Sham
events.title: Amr ibn Luhay goes to Sham
events.desc: He saw the people of Sham worshipping idols and wanted to bring one home.

events.label: Hubal
events.title: Hubal is set at the Kaaba
events.desc: The Meccans were shocked to find an idol before the Kaaba.

events.label: Spreading
events.title: Idols spread through the Hajj
events.desc: Distant tribes carried home new idols such as Lat, Uzza and Manat.

events.label: Five idols
events.title: Nuh's five idols are dug up
events.desc: The idols of righteous men were dug up and carried to various regions.

events.label: Hira
events.title: The Prophet SAW in the Cave of Hira
events.desc: In that darkness he reflected on Jabal Nur.

lessons.title: Manners of entering the mosque
lessons.body: Enter with the right foot and recite the supplication that Allah open the doors of mercy.

lessons.title: The Kaaba is a qibla, not an object of worship
lessons.body: We face the Kaaba but worship Allah alone.

lessons.title: Worshipping the Lord who created us
lessons.body: What human hands make is not worthy of worship. We worship the Lord who created us.

lessons.title: Following a leader without knowledge misleads
lessons.body: People without knowledge followed whatever their leader said and were misled.

lessons.title: Excessive veneration of the righteous
lessons.body: Statues of righteous people made to remember them ended up worshipped.

lessons.title: Good character spreads Islam
lessons.body: Muslim traders showed good character until many embraced Islam in the Malay world.

lessons.title: Knowledge distinguishes humans
lessons.body: Without knowledge humans are no different from animals.

lessons.title: The Quran is light
lessons.body: The Quran was sent down in Ramadan to illuminate the darkness of ignorance.
